clientSettings.title: Client Settings
clientSettings.description: Configure client behavior and request handling.
clientSettings.dropExcessRequestsHelp: If enabled, Bifrost will drop requests that exceed pool capacity.
clientSettings.disableDbPings: Disable DB Pings in Health Check
clientSettings.disableDbPingsHelp: If enabled, the /health endpoint will skip database connectivity checks and return OK immediately.
clientSettings.dumpErrorsHelp: If enabled, full error details are written to the server console logs. Useful for debugging, but may be noisy in production.
clientSettings.asyncJobTtlHelp: Default time-to-live for async job results in seconds. Results are automatically cleaned up after expiry.
clientSettings.languageHelp: Display language for the dashboard. Saved in this browser and applied right away.
clientSettings.headerForwardingHelp: Control which extra headers are forwarded to LLM providers.
clientSettings.prefixedHeaders: <span0>Prefixed headers:</span0> Use  <code1>x-bf-eh-*</code1> prefix. For example,  <code2>x-bf-eh-custom-id</code2> is forwarded as  <code3>custom-id</code3>.
clientSettings.prefixedHeadersHelp: Use x-bf-eh-* prefix. For example, x-bf-eh-custom-id is forwarded as custom-id.
clientSettings.directHeaders: <span0>Direct headers:</span0> Any header explicitly added to the allowlist can be forwarded directly without the prefix (e.g.,  <code1>anthropic-beta</code1>).
clientSettings.directHeadersHelp: Any header explicitly added to the allowlist can be forwarded directly without the prefix (e.g., anthropic-beta).
clientSettings.allowlistEmptyHelp: Only x-bf-eh-* prefixed headers are forwarded (default behavior)
clientSettings.allowlistConfiguredHelp: Prefixed headers filtered by allowlist, plus any direct header in the allowlist is forwarded
clientSettings.denylistRuleHelp: Headers in the denylist are always blocked from forwarding
clientSettings.wildcardsHelp: Use * at the end of a pattern to match prefixes (e.g., anthropic-* matches all headers starting with anthropic-). Use * alone to match all headers.
clientSettings.importantWithoutPrefix: Allowlist/denylist entries should be the header name without the x-bf-eh- prefix
clientSettings.importantExample: Example: To allow x-bf-eh-custom-id or direct custom-id, add custom-id to the allowlist
clientSettings.securityNoteBody: Some headers are always blocked for security reasons regardless of configuration. These headers cannot be added to the allowlist or denylist:
clientSettings.allowlistHelp: Headers to allow. Enter names without the <code0>x-bf-eh-</code0> prefix. Any header in this list can also be sent directly without the prefix.
clientSettings.denylistHelp: Headers to block. Enter names without the <code0>x-bf-eh-</code0> prefix. Applies to both prefixed and direct header forwarding.
clientSettings.toastMinBytes: All byte values must be at least 1024 (1 KB).
clientSettings.toastMaxVsRequest: Max payload size must be greater than or equal to the request threshold.
clientSettings.toastMaxVsResponse: Max payload size must be greater than or equal to the response threshold.
clientSettings.toastSaveLargePayloadFailed: Failed to save large payload config: {{error}}
clientSettings.toastSavedWithRestart: Settings updated. Large payload changes require a restart to apply.
clientSettings.droppedRequests_one: Have dropped {{count}} request since last restart.
clientSettings.droppedRequests_other: Have dropped {{count}} requests since last restart.
clientSettings.emptyAllowlist: <span0>Allowlist empty:</span0> Only  <code1>x-bf-eh-*</code1> prefixed headers are forwarded (default behavior)
clientSettings.configuredAllowlist: <span0>Allowlist configured:</span0> Prefixed headers filtered by allowlist, plus any direct header in the allowlist is forwarded
clientSettings.denylistRules: <span0>Denylist:</span0> Headers in the denylist are always blocked from forwarding
clientSettings.wildcardRules: <span0>Wildcards:</span0> Use  <code1>*</code1> at the end of a pattern to match prefixes (e.g., <code2>anthropic-*</code2> matches all headers starting with <code3>anthropic-</code3>). Use  <code4>*</code4> alone to match all headers.
clientSettings.headerNames: Allowlist/denylist entries should be the header name <span0>without</span0> the  <code1>x-bf-eh-</code1> prefix
clientSettings.allowlistExample: Example: To allow <code0>x-bf-eh-custom-id</code0> or direct  <code1>custom-id</code1>, add  <code2>custom-id</code2> to the allowlist
clientSettings.extraFieldsPlacementHelp: Where inference responses carry Bifrost's extra_fields metadata. Body keeps the extra_fields object in the JSON response. Headers removes it from the body and from every streaming chunk, and sends its scalar fields as x-bifrost-* response headers.
clientSettings.extraFieldsPlacementDroppedNote: In Headers mode these fields are dropped and not sent anywhere: raw request, raw response, routing metadata, guardrail debug, parse errors, and on errors key statuses, billed usage and MCP auth details. Streaming responses only carry what is known before the first chunk (routing, fallback, cache lookup), so per-chunk latency, chunk index and final totals are dropped too.

caching.title: Local Cache
caching.description: Cache responses locally with two complementary lookup paths: direct hash matching for exact replays, and semantic similarity search for related content.
caching.enableHelp: Loads (or unloads) the plugin without a server restart. Configuration changes you make below mutate the live plugin in place, no redeploy needed.
caching.directHelp: Direct-only mode hashes each request and replays an exact match. No embeddings, no provider needed. Cheapest path, perfect for stable prompts.
caching.semanticHelp: Direct + semantic mode adds vector similarity search on top of direct hash matching. Requires an embedding-capable provider and the model's real dimension. Direct hits are still served first; semantic search runs only when the direct lookup misses.
caching.structuralChangeHelp: <b0>Heads up:</b0> a vector store namespace can only hold vectors of <em1>one</em1> dimension. Whenever you change the embedding <b2>provider</b2>, <b3>model</b3>, or <b4>dimension</b4>, make sure the <b5>dimension</b5> still matches what the model produces, otherwise writes to the existing namespace will fail and reads will silently miss. The namespace is <em6>not</em6> recreated automatically; either use a fresh namespace or drop the existing class/index in your vector store before saving.
caching.inheritedKeysHelp: API keys are inherited from the embedding provider's main configuration, you don't need to add them again here.
caching.dimensionHelp: Vector size produced by the embedding model. Must match the model exactly (e.g. <code0>1536</code0> for OpenAI <code1>text-embedding-3-small</code1>, <code2>3072</code2> for <code3>text-embedding-3-large</code3>, <code4>768</code4> for many Cohere/Voyage models).
caching.ttlHelp: How long cached entries live before they expire. Override per-request via the <b0>x-bf-cache-ttl</b0> header.
caching.thresholdHelp: Minimum cosine similarity for a semantic hit. Override per-request via <b0>x-bf-cache-threshold</b0>.
caching.namespaceHelp: Bucket/index name where cache entries live. Leave blank to use the default (<code0>BifrostSemanticCachePlugin</code0>). Changing this points the plugin at a different (possibly empty) bucket. Old entries are not deleted, they just stop being queried.
caching.defaultKeyHelp: Fallback partition key used when a request doesn't set <b0>x-bf-cache-key</b0>. Cache keys isolate entries: same key ↔ shared cache pool. Leave blank to <b1>disable caching</b1> for any request that doesn't send the header.
caching.conversationThresholdHelp: Skip caching for conversations with more than this many messages. Long histories rarely match exactly and inflate the cache without paying off.
caching.cacheByModelHelp: Include model name in the cache key. Different models won't share cached responses.
caching.cacheByProviderHelp: Include provider name in the cache key. Different providers won't share cached responses.

overrides.key: <b0>x-bf-cache-key</b0>: scope this request to a specific cache partition.
overrides.ttl: <b0>x-bf-cache-ttl</b0>: override TTL for just this request.
overrides.type: <b0>x-bf-cache-type</b0>: send <code1>direct</code1> or <code2>semantic</code2> to limit lookup to one path.
overrides.noStore: <b0>x-bf-cache-no-store</b0>: <code1>true</code1> to skip writing the response (still serves cached hits).

caching.excludeSystemPromptHelp: Strip system messages from the cache key.
caching.semanticProviderRequired: Configure an embedding-capable provider to enable semantic mode.
caching.searchEmbeddingModel: Search or type an embedding model...
caching.unexpectedError: An unexpected error occurred. Please try again.

validation.provider: Pick an embedding provider for semantic mode, or switch to Direct only.
validation.model: Pick an embedding model for semantic mode.
validation.dimension: Semantic mode requires the embedding model's real dimension (must be > 1).
validation.threshold: Similarity threshold must be between 0 and 1.
validation.conversationThreshold: Conversation history threshold must be between 1 and 50.

caching.scopeByIdentityHelp: Serve a cached response only to the virtual key and user that wrote it. Turn off to share entries across identities that send the same cache key.

security.title: Security Settings
security.description: Configure security and access control settings.
security.setupTokenHelp: Enter the setup token configured by your operator to create the first admin account. It's set via setup_token in config.json or the BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN environment variable.
security.setupTokenPlaceholder: Paste the setup token configured by your operator
security.enableAuthHelp: Require authentication (virtual key, API key, or user token) for all inference endpoints.
security.enforceVkHelp: Require a virtual key for all inference requests.
security.allowedHeadersHelp: Comma-separated list of allowed headers for CORS.
security.toastInvalidOrigins: Invalid origins: {{origins}}. Origins must be valid URLs like https://example.com, wildcard patterns like https://*.example.com, or "*" to allow all origins
security.toastInvalidCooldown: Rotation cooldown must be a duration like "30s", "5m", or "1h30m" (leave empty to disable).
security.vkRotationCooldownDesc: After rotating a virtual key, the previous value keeps authenticating for this long, giving callers time to switch to the new key. Use a duration like 30s, 5m, or 1h. Leave empty (or 0) to have the old value stop working immediately. Maximum 30 days.
security.authTypeUnavailable: Could not load authentication type. Dashboard password settings are hidden until this request succeeds.
security.passwordProtectHelp: Set up authentication credentials to protect your Bifrost dashboard. Once configured, use the generated token for all admin API calls.
security.passwordPolicyHelp: Use at least 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. Env var references are accepted.
security.oauthIssuerUrlHelp: Stable public URL of Bifrost's OAuth authorization server, advertised in discovery documents and set as the <code0>iss</code0> claim of every token Bifrost issues. MCP OAuth (required in OAuth and Both modes) and Cross App Access use it. Bifrost never derives it from the request <code1>Host</code1> header, because that header is caller-controlled. Supports env var syntax (e.g. <code2>env.BIFROST_ISSUER_URL</code2>).
security.issuerChangeWarning: Changing the issuer invalidates the access tokens Bifrost has issued. MCP clients refresh them automatically, and Cross App Access apps request new ones.
security.toastIssuerUrlRequired: Issuer URL is required while MCP auth mode is OAuth or Both. Switch MCP auth to Headers in MCP Settings to clear it.
security.firstSetupHelp: No admin account exists yet, so management APIs only accept the setup token. Enter the token configured via <code0>setup_token</code0> in <code1>config.json</code1> (or the <code2>BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN</code2> environment variable) to create the admin account. Once it is enabled, the setup token stops working.
security.dualCredentialHelp: How to handle inference requests that present both an identity provider access token (<b0>Authorization: Bearer</b0>) and a virtual key (<b1>x-bf-vk</b1>). <b2>Prefer IDP token</b2> uses the user token for identity, <b3>Prefer virtual key</b3> drops the IDP token and authenticates via the virtual key, and <b4>Reject request</b4> returns a 400 error.
security.directKeysHelp: When enabled, callers can pass a provider API key directly in the <b0>Authorization</b0>, <b1>x-api-key</b1>, or  <b2>x-goog-api-key</b2> header alongside <b3>x-bf-direct-key: true</b3>. Bifrost will use that key directly, bypassing the registered key pool.
security.originsHelp: Comma-separated list of allowed origins for CORS and WebSocket connections. Localhost origins are always allowed. Each origin must be a complete URL with protocol (e.g., https://app.example.com, http://10.0.0.100:3000). Wildcards are supported for subdomains (e.g., https://*.example.com) or use "*" to allow all origins.
security.requiredHeadersHelp: Comma-separated list of headers that must be present on every request. Requests missing any of these headers will be rejected with a 400 error. Header names are case-insensitive.
security.routesHelp: Comma-separated list of routes that bypass the auth middleware. Requests to these routes will not require authentication. System routes like <b0>/health</b0>, <b1>/api/session/login</b1>, and <b2>/api/session/is-auth-enabled</b2> are always whitelisted regardless of this setting.
security.currentPasswordPlaceholder: Enter the admin password currently in use
security.proofHelp: Dashboard protection is switched off, so this session is not signed in. Turning it back on or changing the admin credentials requires the admin password that is currently stored.
security.useSetupTokenInstead: ...or confirm with a setup token instead
security.setupTokenAlternativeHelp: If the current password is not at hand, the <code0>setup_token</code0> from <code1>config.json</code1> (or the <code2>BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN</code2> environment variable) confirms this change too.
security.authorizedBySetupToken: Authorized with the setup token entered on the setup screen. Saving creates the admin account, after which the setup token stops working.
security.setupVirtualKeyHelp: to set up a virtual key before enabling this. Calls without a valid credential will return 401.
security.inferenceAuthOffWarning: The dashboard is authentication protected, but this is a separate control: anyone who can reach this gateway can still call inference endpoints (e.g. chat completions) with no credential at all, spending your provider budget and reading provider-side state your key has access to. Turn this on unless you've deliberately chosen to leave inference open.
security.deleteExpiredVirtualKeysHelp: When enabled, a daily cleanup job deletes every virtual key whose expiry has passed and posts a notification listing the removed keys. Each key can override this from its <b0>Delete after expire</b0> switch: a key set to off is kept, and a key set to on is deleted even while this is disabled.
security.enforceVkObjectOwnership: Restrict Provider Objects to the Creating Virtual Key
security.enforceVkObjectOwnershipHelp: When enabled, files, batches, videos, containers, cached contents and live sessions created with a virtual key can only be read, listed or deleted with that same key. Other virtual keys get a not-found error and do not see them in lists. Requests without a virtual key are not affected. The creating key is recorded even while this is disabled, so enabling it again also covers objects created in the meantime, except any whose creating key could not be recorded.
security.proofRequired: Enter the current admin password to confirm this change. Dashboard protection is off, so this session is not signed in. If you do not know the password, use the setup token instead.
security.skipAccessProfileKeyCreation: Don't Create User Virtual Keys for Access Profiles
security.skipAccessProfileKeyCreationHelp: When enabled, a user's first access profile doesn't create a virtual key for them. Keys the user already owns, or that you add for them, are still governed by the profile while they hold one.
security.skipAccessProfileKeyDeletion: Don't Delete User Virtual Keys When Access Profiles Are Removed
security.skipAccessProfileKeyDeletionHelp: When enabled, removing a user's last access profile keeps their virtual keys as ordinary keys, with none of the profile's providers or access. Deleting the user still deletes their keys.

logging.title: Logs Settings
logging.description: Configure logging settings for requests and responses.
logging.enableLogsHelp: Enable logging of requests and responses to a SQL database. This can add 40-60mb of overhead to the system memory.
logging.requiresStore: Requires logs store to be configured and enabled in config.json.
logging.disableContentLoggingHelp: Applies to LLM, MCP, agent and relay logs. When enabled, only usage metadata (latency, cost, token count, status, routing IDs, etc.) is logged. Request/response content (messages, params, tool calls, and any raw provider bytes) is dropped from log records, even when <code0>store_raw_request_response</code0> is on. Raw-byte send-back to callers via <code1>send_back_raw_*</code1> is unaffected. Agent protocol bodies follow this setting; upstream raw captures also require Capture Raw Request and Response in Agent Gateway settings.
logging.retainContentHelp: When enabled, requests with content logging disabled (via the global setting above or the x-bf-disable-content-logging header) still have their full content offloaded to object storage, but the content is never shown in logs: the database row stays metadata-only and the UI/API never fetch the payload back. Content is then only readable with direct access to the storage bucket. When disabled, content for such requests is dropped entirely (current behavior).
logging.requiresObjectStorage: Requires object storage to be configured on the logs store in config.json.
logging.allowContentOverrideHelp: When enabled, individual requests can override the global content logging setting using the x-bf-disable-content-logging header or context key, and can opt-in to persisting raw provider bytes in logs using the x-bf-store-raw-request-response header. Raw-byte storage requires content logging to be on, either globally, or via x-bf-disable-content-logging: false on the same request. If content logging is off, raw bytes are dropped from the log record even when x-bf-store-raw-request-response: true. Does not control sending raw bytes back to callers; see {{setting}}.
logging.allowRawOverrideHelp: When enabled, individual requests can send raw provider request/response bytes back to the caller using the x-bf-send-back-raw-request and x-bf-send-back-raw-response headers. Does not affect log storage; raw-byte persistence in logs is controlled by {{setting}}.
logging.logRetentionDaysHelp: Number of days to retain logs in the database. Minimum is 1 day. Older logs will be automatically deleted.
logging.hideDeletedVks: Do Not Show Deleted VirtualKeys In Filters
logging.hideDeletedVksHelp: When enabled, deleted virtual keys are excluded from Virtual Keys filter options in Logs, Dashboard, and MCP Logs.
logging.loggingHeadersHelp: Comma-separated list of request headers to capture in log metadata. Supports exact names and wildcard patterns (e.g. x-custom-* captures all headers with that prefix, * logs all headers; note that * will capture sensitive headers like Authorization). Values are extracted from incoming requests and stored in the metadata field of log entries. Headers with the x-bf-lh- prefix are always captured automatically. Relay Logs carry the same metadata, and beside it the headers a relay's routes match on; no other header, and never the reply's, is stored.
logging.toastRetentionMin: Log retention days must be at least 1 day
logging.hiddenRequestTypesHelp: Selected request types are still logged but excluded from Logs and Dashboard views, including counts, charts and filter options. Streaming and non-streaming types are separate. Leave empty to show every request type. Takes effect on the next request, no restart needed. Can also be set with
logging.hiddenRequestTypesLoadError: Unable to load hidden request types.

observability.prometheusLabelsHelp: Comma-separated list of custom labels to add to the Prometheus metrics.
observability.toastNotLoaded: Could not save settings: configuration not loaded.

performance.title: Performance Tuning
performance.maxRequestBodySizeHelp: Maximum size of request body in megabytes.
performance.toastPoolPositive: Initial pool size must be a positive number.
performance.toastBodyPositive: Max request body size must be a positive number.

compatibility.title: Compatibility
compatibility.description: Configure request conversions and compatibility fallbacks.
compatibility.convertTextToChatHelp: Convert text completion requests to chat for models that only support chat.
compatibility.convertChatToResponsesHelp: Convert chat completion requests to responses for models that only support responses.
compatibility.dropUnsupportedParamsHelp: Drop unsupported parameters based on model catalog allowlist.
compatibility.convertUnsupportedParamsHelp: Converts model parameter values that are not supported by the model.
compatibility.azureDeepseek: Use Chat Completion APIs for Azure Deepseek models
compatibility.azureDeepseekHelp: Use Chat Completion APIs for Claude Code, Codex, etc. for Azure Deepseek models.
compatibility.forceReasoningOnlyToResponses: Use Responses API for reasoning only OpenAI models
compatibility.forceReasoningOnlyToResponsesHelp: Route chat completion requests to the Responses API for models that cannot reason with tool calls on chat completions, instead of turning reasoning off.
compatibility.convertDecisionToResponses: Emulate Decisions API on non-decision models
compatibility.convertDecisionToResponsesHelp: Answer decision requests for models without a native decisions endpoint by prompting the model through the Responses API with a forced function tool. When off, those requests fail as unsupported.

featureFlags.title: Feature Flags
featureFlags.description: Toggle in-process feature flags. Flags are declared in code; values can also be set via config.json or Helm, in which case they appear here as locked.
featureFlags.lockedHelp: Value is pinned by config.json or Helm; edit your config to change it.
featureFlags.enterpriseHelp: This flag gates an enterprise-only feature. Upgrade to enable it.
featureFlags.unregisteredHelp: This id has no code registration. Restore the Register() call or clean up the stale value.
featureFlags.unregisteredNote: No code currently reads this flag. The override is stored but inert until a Register() call is added.

mcpSettings.title: MCP Settings
mcpSettings.description: Configure MCP (Model Context Protocol) agent and tool settings.
mcpSettings.maxAgentDepthHelp: Maximum depth for MCP agent execution.
mcpSettings.toolTimeoutHelp: Maximum time in seconds for tool execution.
mcpSettings.issuerUrlRequiredModes: Required in OAuth and Both modes.
mcpSettings.toastDepthPositive: Max agent depth must be a positive number.
mcpSettings.toastTimeoutPositive: Tool execution timeout must be a positive number.
mcpSettings.toastAuthCodeTtl: Authorization code TTL must be between 1 and 900 seconds (15 minutes).
mcpSettings.toastAccessTokenTtl: Access token TTL must be at least 60 seconds.
mcpSettings.maxDepthHelp: Maximum depth for MCP agent execution.
mcpSettings.refreshIntervalHelp: How often to refresh tool lists from MCP servers. Set to 0 to use the default of 10 minutes.
mcpSettings.disableAutoToolInjectionHelp: When enabled, MCP tools are not automatically included in every request. Tools are only injected when explicitly specified via request headers (<code0>x-bf-mcp-include-tools</code0>) and still must be allowed by the virtual key MCP configuration.
mcpSettings.tempTokenHelp: When enabled, per-user MCP OAuth links can include a short-lived scoped token so someone without an active Bifrost dashboard session can complete the flow. Keep disabled to require normal dashboard authentication.
mcpSettings.bindingHelp: How tools are exposed in the VFS: server-level (all tools per server) or tool-level (individual tools).
mcpSettings.externalClientUrlHelp: Override Bifrost's public base URL when it runs behind a reverse proxy. <b0>Leave blank to derive the URL</b0> from the incoming <code1>Host</code1> header. Used as the <code2>redirect_uri</code2> Bifrost registers with upstream OAuth providers when it acts as a client to an MCP server (e.g. Notion or Jira redirect the browser to <code3><URL>/api/oauth/callback</code3> after login). Supports env var syntax (e.g.  <code4>env.BIFROST_EXTERNAL_URL</code4>).
mcpSettings.externalClientUrlWarningHelp: Upstream OAuth providers lock the <code0>redirect_uri</code0> to whatever was registered initially, so MCP clients that already completed OAuth will fail with <em1>"Invalid redirect URI"</em1>. To recover, clear the stored OAuth client credentials for the affected MCP servers and re-authorize so Bifrost re-runs Dynamic Client Registration with the new URL.
mcpSettings.authModeHelp: Controls how inbound MCP clients (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor) authenticate to the <code0>/mcp</code0>  endpoint. <b1>headers</b1> (default) - VK / api-key / session headers only, OAuth discovery disabled. <b2>both</b2> - accepts header credentials and Bifrost-issued JWTs; existing integrations are unaffected. <b3>oauth</b3> - JWTs only; VK and header access is disabled.
mcpSettings.issuerUrlHelp: Stable public URL advertised in discovery documents and embedded as the <code0>iss</code0> claim in every JWT. Required in OAuth and Both modes: Bifrost never derives the issuer from the request <code1>Host</code1> header, because that header is caller-controlled. Supports env var syntax (e.g. <code2>env.BIFROST_ISSUER_URL</code2>).
mcpSettings.authCodeTtlHelp: How long the one-time code is valid after the consent page redirects back to the MCP client (default: 300, max 900 = 15 min).
mcpSettings.accessTokenTtlHelp: Lifetime of issued JWT Bearer tokens. Clients silently refresh when expired (default: 600 = 10 min). Also bounds how long a revoked grant keeps working before it is cut off.
mcpSettings.requireIdpLoginHelp: When enabled, the OAuth consent flow only offers identity-provider login. Virtual keys can no longer be used to obtain an MCP token, and existing virtual-key OAuth sessions lose access immediately. Anonymous session access is unaffected (controlled by Enforce Authentication on Inference).
mcpSettings.allToolsPerServerInASinglePyFile: All tools per server in a single .py file
mcpSettings.externalClientUrlWarning: Changing this URL can break existing MCP clients
mcpSettings.headerAccessDisabled: VK / header MCP access will be disabled
mcpSettings.headerAccessDisabledHelp: All existing MCP integrations that use a virtual key, api-key, or session header will stop working immediately. Clients must re-authenticate via the OAuth consent flow to obtain a JWT before they can connect.
mcpSettings.oauthDiscoveryDisabledHelp: All MCP clients that authenticated via the OAuth consent flow will lose access; their JWTs will be rejected and their refresh tokens will become unusable. They will need to reconfigure using a virtual key or api-key header.
mcpSettings.bothAuthModesHelp: Existing VK / header integrations continue to work unchanged. New MCP clients can connect via OAuth - they'll be redirected to the consent page to pick an identity.
mcpSettings.virtualKeyOauthDisabled: Virtual-key MCP access via OAuth will stop
mcpSettings.virtualKeyOauthDisabledHelp: MCP clients that authenticated with a virtual key will lose access immediately and must sign in through your identity provider to reconnect.
mcpSettings.toastSyncIntervalInvalid: Tool sync interval must be zero or a positive number.
mcpSettings.toastMaxInstructionsPerServerInvalid: Max instruction length per server must be zero or a positive number.
mcpSettings.toastMaxInstructionsTotalInvalid: Max instruction length total must be zero or a positive number.
mcpSettings.toastIssuerUrlRequired: Issuer URL is required when MCP auth mode is OAuth or Both. Set it in Settings > Security first.
mcpSettings.oauthPrivateAllowlistHelp: Hosts, IP addresses, or CIDR ranges (no scheme or port) that OAuth discovery, client registration, and token requests for MCP servers may reach when they resolve to a loopback or private address, e.g. <code0>localhost</code0>, <code1>127.0.0.1</code1>, or <code2>10.20.0.0/16</code2>. Applies to MCP servers added with dashboard authentication enabled; changing it requires dashboard authentication. Link-local and cloud metadata addresses are always blocked.
mcpSettings.oauthPrivateAllowlistPlaceholder: Add host, IP, or CIDR (Enter or comma)
mcpSettings.maxInstructionsPerServerHelp: Longer text is truncated with a notice. Set to 0 to use the default of 4096.
mcpSettings.maxProtocolVersionHelp: Newest MCP protocol version Bifrost offers to MCP servers. Auto uses the latest Bifrost supports. Each server can override this.
mcpSettings.maxInstructionsTotalHelp: Ceiling across every server a caller can see. At <code0>Gateway and LLM requests</code0> this rides on every MCP-bearing request, so raising it raises per-request tokens. Set to 0 to use the default of 16384.
mcpSettings.allowedRedirectUrisHelp: Exact callback URIs remote MCP clients may use, e.g. <code0>https://www.cursor.com/agents/mcp/oauth/callback</code0>. Add <code1>*</code1> to allow any https callback; partial wildcards are not supported. Loopback callbacks and <code2>cursor://anysphere.cursor-mcp</code2> are always allowed. Changing this list requires dashboard authentication.
mcpSettings.anyCallbackAllowedHelp: Any MCP client can register with a callback on any host, so the consent page is the only check against a client that sends authorization codes to an attacker. Prefer listing exact callback URIs.
mcpSettings.codeModeLimitsDescription: Limits on each code execution. Leave a field empty to use its default. Executions are not limited in how many run at once.
mcpSettings.limitMaxSourceBytesDesc: Largest code a single execution may submit.
mcpSettings.limitMaxStepsDesc: Interpreter steps per execution, including work inside builtins.

topics.title: Topic clusters
topics.infoIntro: Topics group requests by what was asked, so Warp can answer what people ask about.
topics.infoSeed: <b0>1. Seed, once.</b0> A one-time run clusters the indexed requests of a window and names each group. Seeding is once per embedding model.
topics.infoFiled: <b0>2. Filed as they arrive.</b0> Every request indexed after that is filed under its nearest topic.
topics.infoFound: <b0>3. New topics found.</b0> Requests that match no topic wait. Once the new topic threshold is reached, an hourly pass groups them into new topics or folds them into existing ones.
topics.infoTidy: <b0>4. Kept tidy.</b0> The same pass retires topics with no requests for 30 days and merges topics that come to mean the same thing.
topics.infoReseed: Changing the embedding model starts over: its topics are seeded again.
topics.description: Seed topics once from a window of indexed requests. After that they keep themselves up to date as new requests are indexed, with no further runs.
topics.seeded: Topics are built for this embedding model and keep themselves up to date: new requests are filed as they are indexed, and new topics are found among the ones that match none.
topics.saveBeforeSeed: Save configuration changes before seeding topics.
topics.needsBackfill: Nothing is indexed for this embedding model yet. Backfill a window above first, then seed topics from the same window.

topics.thresholdHint: How many requests that matched no topic have to be waiting before Warp groups them into new topics, checked hourly. Lower finds new subjects sooner from fewer examples; higher waits for clearer patterns. {{min}} to {{max}}.
topics.thresholdError: Must be a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}

job.title: Async Job
job.enableLabel: This route starts an async job
job.enableInfo: For APIs that reply with a job id and bill when the work finishes. The route is then always buffered.
job.step1: The start call is relayed and billed like any call.
job.step2: Bifrost reads the job id from its reply.
job.step3: It sends the poll request, with the job id in place of {{token}}, until the status is terminal.
job.step4: A succeeded job is priced with the job pricing below and charged to the caller once.
job.idPathInfo: Where the start call's reply carries the job id, as a gjson path.
job.pollInfo: The request that reports where the job stands. {{token}} in the path, a header value or the body is replaced with the job id.
job.statusPathInfo: Where the poll reply carries the job status, as a gjson path.
job.succeededInfo: Comma-separated statuses that end the job with work to bill.
job.failedInfo: Comma-separated statuses that end the job at no further charge.
job.timeoutInfo: A job still running after this long is dropped without a further charge.
job.pricingInfo: Applied to the final poll reply of a succeeded job, such as pages processed. Empty fields inherit the route pricing; the fee is charged only if set here, since the start call already paid it.

credentials.authInfo: How the gateway authenticates to the upstream. Callers never send this credential; they authenticate to Bifrost with a virtual key.
credentials.headerNameInfo: The request header that carries the credential, such as X-API-Key.
credentials.valuePrefixInfo: Text put before the credential in the header, such as Token followed by a space.
credentials.queryParamInfo: The query parameter that carries the credential, such as api_key.
credentials.credentialInfo: Stored encrypted and never sent by callers; the gateway adds it to every relayed request.
credentials.awsServiceInfo: The SigV4 signing name, such as textract, translate or s3.
credentials.awsMethodInfo: IAM Role uses the credentials of the environment Bifrost runs in (instance role, IRSA, env vars). Explicit uses the keys entered here.
credentials.iamRoleInfo: Uses IAM roles attached to your environment (EC2, Lambda, ECS, EKS).
credentials.regionInfo: The AWS region requests are signed for, such as us-east-1.
credentials.roleArnInfo: Assume an IAM role before requests. Works with both explicit credentials and inherited IAM (EC2, ECS, EKS).
credentials.externalIdInfo: Required by the role's trust policy when using cross-account access

endpointConfig.descriptionInfo: Shown in the relay list; for your team only.
endpointConfig.anyPathInfo: Relay requests that match no route instead of refusing them with 404. Unrouted POSTs use the relay pricing.
endpointConfig.anyPathWarning: Every path on the upstream is reachable with this relay's credential. Prefer listing routes.
endpointConfig.pricingInfo: The default price of a counted call. Routes can override any field. The cost is charged to the caller's virtual key, team and customer budgets.
endpointConfig.streamPathsInfo: One route glob per line; matching paths are always relayed as streams. Otherwise an event-stream reply from the upstream is streamed and anything else is read and priced.
endpointConfig.costPathInfo: A USD cost the upstream reports; added to the formula.
endpointConfig.modelPathInfo: Where the model is read from, for the logs.
endpointConfig.modelSourceInfo: Whether Model Path names a field of the request body (the default) or a query parameter, as Deepgram's ?model=.
endpointConfig.ignoreCostInfo: Charge only your fee and unit pricing, never the cost the upstream reports.
endpointConfig.tokensPathInfo: Recorded on Relay Logs, never priced.
endpointConfig.extraHeadersInfo: Sent on every request; a caller's copy of the same header is dropped.
endpointConfig.networkInfo: How Bifrost talks to the upstream directly: request and stream timeouts, the connection pool and TLS trust. To send the traffic through a forward proxy instead, use the Proxy tab.
endpointConfig.timeoutHelp: Longest a buffered call may take, end to end.
endpointConfig.streamIdleHelp: A stream is closed when no data arrives for this long.
endpointConfig.maxConnsHelp: Upper bound on open connections to the upstream.
endpointConfig.insecureInfo: Skip TLS verification of the upstream. Only for self-signed certificates.
endpointConfig.caCertInfo: A CA bundle to trust when the upstream uses a private or self-signed certificate.
endpointConfig.proxyInfo: Sends this relay's outbound traffic through a forward proxy (HTTP, SOCKS5, or the HTTP_PROXY environment). With no proxy set, the global proxy is used when it is enabled for inference. Timeouts and TLS live on the Network tab.
endpointConfig.proxyTypeInfo: HTTP or SOCKS5 sends traffic through the proxy below; Environment uses HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY.
endpointConfig.proxyUrlInfo: The proxy address, or an env. reference to it.
endpointConfig.proxyCaCertInfo: A PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for TLS connections through an SSL-intercepting proxy, or an env. reference to it.
